_meta.description: Thresholds and dispositions for /overwatch (#2768). Externalized so dedupe, rate limiting and finding severity can be tuned without a spec edit (#2318 precedent, same shape as commit-checkpoint-signals.json).

observation.note: The fifteen events are what peer-announce.js broadcasts to every addressable peer (the four branch-operation notices, #2960, reach every peer even under targeted routing), so a discoverable idle session receives them with no new transport. Direct SendMessage between two OTHER sessions is point-to-point and unobservable — the monitor sees only what is addressed to it, and must say so rather than implying wider coverage. This list is enumerated rather than read from the EVENTS object, so a new event is invisible to the monitor until added here (#2781).

findings.description: A Refs #N commit appeared in git log with no work-started announcement from any session.
findings.rationale: A session with groups.work disabled commits legitimately and announces nothing. Filing a bug for a configured-quiet peer would be wrong every time.

findings.description: A work-started announcement with no matching work-completed after the pairing window.
findings.rationale: The peer may still be working. Rule 08 makes every event 1 carry exactly one event 2, so an unmatched opener is worth surfacing but is not by itself a defect.

findings.description: Two in-flight issues declare the same file in their Files to modify sections.
findings.rationale: Overlap is a collision risk, not a defect. Reporting it early is the whole value; filing a bug about it names no broken behaviour. It is the one finding the monitor also sends to the sessions involved, as a targeted overlap notice gated by the overlapNotices lever and bounded by overlapNotices below (#2914).

findings.description: minimize-helper stale reports an output that does not match its recorded hash.
findings.rationale: A concrete, reproducible defect with a named remedy (regenerate, do not edit). The staleness check is the authority, so the finding does not rest on the monitor's own judgment.

findings.description: A guard test fails on the pushed tip while its issue is already closed.
findings.rationale: A failing test on a closed issue is unambiguous and nobody owns it — exactly the gap an unattended observer is positioned to catch.

findings.description: A peer sends an opener — review-started, review-resolved or work-started — while its previous opener of the same kind is still unmatched by that opener's closer.
findings.rationale: The front-loaded batch #2879 observed: every opener of a multi-issue run sent before any verdict. Nothing was lost, so it is not a defect to file, but while it lasts a dropped closer looks exactly like a queued one — the ambiguity #2781 removed. Rule 09 now defines when a turn begins so it should not recur; reporting it makes a recurrence visible instead of relying on someone noticing it by eye.

findings.description: A terminal announcement for an issue is followed by any further announcement naming that same issue. Keys on terminality generally, not on review-passed alone.
findings.rationale: The contradiction is a property of the announcement vocabulary, not of either peer. A forced re-review is legitimate — /review-issue --force is the supported way to re-review, and rule 09 suppresses its review-started opener by design so a nested re-review is not announced as a fresh one. Both halves work as specified; what overclaims is the word terminal, which is true of a review cycle and false of an issue. Filing would blame a session that followed the rules, so this reports. Distinct from opener-while-previous-unmatched, the nearest kind and the one most likely to be mistaken for it: that one fires on an opener whose own closer has not arrived, and is about ordering within a cycle. This one fires after a cycle has CLOSED, on an event that contradicts a claim the closer already made. A run can produce either without the other.

autoCreate.label: auto-filed

dedupe.rationale: A monitor observing a standing condition re-derives the same finding every tick, so without dedupe one condition becomes one issue per tick. Detail is deliberately excluded from the fingerprint: it is the part most likely to be reworded between ticks while the finding is the same one, and including it would defeat dedupe on exactly the findings dedupe exists for. Twelve hours is long enough to cover an unattended overnight run and short enough that a genuinely recurring condition is re-reported the next day.

rateLimit.rationale: Bounds the blast radius of an analysis that goes wrong. Five is well above the number of distinct filable findings a healthy working directory produces in a session, so the cap is invisible in the common case and decisive in the pathological one.

autoCreate.note: A sweep is mandatory before any auto-filed bug and an already-shipped verdict skips the filing. Duplicate filing is a known failure in this repo — the whole --prior-art subsystem exists because of it — and an unattended filer has no human check standing between it and the board.

dedupe.rationale: A scope overlap is a standing condition: it holds for as long as both issues are in flight, and the monitor re-derives it on every tick. Without dedupe one overlap becomes one message per tick to two sessions that were already told. The fingerprint is the recipient, the issue pair and the overlapping path set, so a WIDENED overlap is a new notice while an unchanged one is not. Twelve hours matches autoCreate.dedupe: long enough to cover an unattended run, short enough that an overlap still standing the next day is raised again.

rateLimit.rationale: Bounds how many notices one working session receives in an hour, whatever the monitor's analysis produces. Each notice costs the recipient a turn, and a session drowning in notices stops reading them, which removes the one that mattered. Three distinct overlaps an hour is well above what a healthy working directory produces, so the cap is invisible in the common case.

overlapNotices.note: Whether to send at all is NOT here: it is the overlapNotices lever in .claude/x-session.json, resolved by cross-session-config.js, because .claude/metadata/ is a read-only hub junction in deployed projects and a project must be able to turn notices off. These thresholds only bound a send the lever already allows. Unreadable thresholds refuse every send and fall back to report-only, as autoCreate does (#2914).

enhancementOffers.rationale: A delegated subagent cannot make an offer: framework-dev declares Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, Skill and has no AskUserQuestion. Bug filing is non-interactive and therefore delegable; an enhancement offer is not. The asymmetry is enforced by the tool boundary, not by preference.
